key_insight: In an adversarial time-domain eddy-current example, gauge-penalized H¹ elements can converge to an incorrect state, while mixed H¹/H(Curl) elements yield reasonable results.
engineering_relevance: Electromagnetic simulations should use compatible finite element spaces, because mesh refinement alone may not correct errors from an unsuitable discretization.
method: Review H¹ and H(Curl) elements and their compatibility with Maxwell’s equations.
Construct a physically feasible, adversarial time-domain eddy-current problem in the a–φ formulation.
Compare gauge-penalized H¹ elements with gauge-free mixed scalar/edge H¹/H(Curl) elements under mesh refinement.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports persistent failure of penalized H¹ elements under mesh refinement, contrasted with reasonable results from edge elements, but provides no quantitative error metrics.
watch_item: The demonstration uses an intentionally adversarial problem; it does not establish failure for every H¹-based electromagnetic simulation.
paper_title: A time-domain adversarial example demonstrating the failure of $H^1$ elements in $a$-$φ$ electromagnetic simulation
